subject: Possible to have multiple outputs passed to a single uiOutput using a single renderUI function?

messages.author: 0bc357a2b8347256
messages.subject: Possible to have multiple outputs passed to a single uiOutput using a single renderUI function?
parts:
I've found some peripherally related questions in the group, but no definitive answer to this.  Say I've got this in the mainPanel of ui.r:

uiOutput("out1")

can I then in server.r do something like this?

output$out1 = renderUI ({
     tableOutput("tableOut"),
     plotOutput("plotOut")
})

Obviously, this doesn't work (the comma throws an error), but is there a way to accomplish what I'm trying to do here?  I read somewhere that you can have renderUI return a list, but I'm not sure how that list should be formatted.  Any help would be useful.

Thanks!

parts:
I believe you should be able to wrap them together in a tagList:

output$out1 = renderUI ({
  tagList(

})



Some general comments about understanding HTML output from Shiny code:

For outputs (and other HTML tag-generating functions), you can see the HTML they create by running them at the R console:
> plotOutput('foo')
[1] "<div id=\"foo\" class=\"shiny-plot-output\" style=\"width: 100% ; height: 400px\"></div>"
attr(,"html")
[1] TRUE

This output escapes some characters and includes some extra information about the data structures. For cleaner-looking output, you can wrap it in cat(format(...)):
> cat(format(plotOutput('foo')))
<div id="foo" class="shiny-plot-output" style="width: 100% ; height: 400px"></div>

So here's what you get when you wrap two of these things in tagList():
> cat(format( tagList(plotOutput('foo'), tableOutput('foo2')) ))
<div id="foo" class="shiny-plot-output" style="width: 100% ; height: 400px"></div>
<div id="foo2" class="shiny-html-output"></div>


-Winston
